did_you_know.text: The exact identity of Molech is debated: it may have been a deity, or the name of a ritual involving child sacrifice. In either case, the Bible presents the act as a grave offense against the community and the sanctity of life.

Ov and yiddeoni are ancient terms connected with seeking information from the dead or through divination. The prohibition teaches that, in Israelite belief, not every source of knowledge was considered legitimate.
In the Bible, holiness means not only spiritual purity but also being set apart and living according to a purpose. That is why the verse connects becoming holy with keeping the laws.

The expression “his blood is upon him” is a biblical legal formula meaning that the responsibility for the blood penalty rests on the offender. A similar expression appears in other laws in the chapter.
The law treats adultery as a violation of an existing marriage, so it mentions both the man and the woman. In the Bible, marriage is viewed as a social and family bond, not only as a private matter.
The phrase “the land will vomit you out” personifies the land as a body unable to tolerate corrupt behavior. The same image appears in chapter 18, linking the two chapters.

“A land flowing with milk and honey” is a poetic expression for abundance and fertility, not a description of rivers made of milk and honey. In the Bible, honey may refer to bee honey or to a sweet natural syrup such as date syrup.
The distinction between clean and unclean is not the same as the modern distinction between healthy and dirty. These are categories of ritual and dietary law, discussed at length in chapter 11.

The chapter first mentions consulting ovot and yiddeonim in verse 6 and returns to the subject at its close. This repetition emphasizes the Torah’s rejection of attempts to bypass a direct relationship with God.
